utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. Could the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And the appearances of the parties, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Schomburg is unfortunately still ill and unable to come to Court. Considering that there are still Defence witnesses in The Hague who are waiting to testify, it is in the interest of justice for Judge Argibay and I to continue sitting under Rule 15 bis to hear these remaining witnesses even in the absence of Judge Schomburg. Yesterday, we proceeded on the basis of the consent which the parties had given on 10 March for Judge Argibay and I to continue to sitting under Rule 15 bis in the absence of Judge Schomburg. It would apply until it was withdrawn by one or other party or by Dr. Stakic himself. However, for the record, I would again ask that both parties and Dr. Stakic himself formally register their consent to this procedure for today's hearing, 12th of March, year 2003. Starting with the Prosecution, Mr. Koumjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution consents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Defence consents, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have no objections, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, considering that Judge Schomburg is still not available to sit in this case today because he continues to be ill, Judge Argibay and I, being satisfied that it is in the interest of justice to do so, and again based on the consent of the parties and Dr. Stakic himself, hereby order pursuant to Rule 15 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence that for today, the hearing continue in the absence of Judge Schomburg. Let us first deal with the Defence witnesses to be called for the next week. Madam Registrar, can we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. The next matter is the Defence request to admit under Rule 92 bis the statement of Dr. Pavle Nikolic, an expert who testified in the case of Prosecutor versus Simic. Yesterday we heard from the Prosecution that they would be willing to accept the admission into evidence of his statement without cross-examination of Dr. Nikolic provided that the examination and cross-examination of Mr. Pavle Nikolic in the Simic case was also entered into evidence. The Chamber considers that this be a fair solution. Therefore, I would ask that the Defence tender Dr. Pavle Nikolic's report and that the Prosecution tender the testimony of Dr. Nikolic in the Simic case in lieu of cross-examining Dr. Nikolic. Does either party have any objection to following this procedure?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Defence does not have any objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. I would, therefore, ask the Defence to tender the report of Dr. Pavle Nikolic which was filed in our case on 6 March this year with the registry, page numbers D14917, D15057 into evidence. This report is admitted into evidence as Exhibit D90. Does the Prosecution have copies of the testimony of Dr. Pavle Nikolic from the Simic case available?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We will have it at the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. Then I understand that after the break, you'll provide these documents, and then we'll admit those documents as evidence on the part of the Prosecution. Okay. The final matter: I would like to address to the issue which relates to the Defence exhibits. The Defence has asked that it be permitted to amend its original exhibit list dated 18th November, year 2002, in order to add certain documents to that list. Yes? On 3rd March, year 2003, it filed a motion attaching the documents it wished to add to the original list. The Chamber hereby grants the Defence the right to amend its exhibit list to include those exhibits where English translation have already been provided. The Chamber will rule later in relation to those exhibits where no English translation has been provided. Therefore, all the exhibits attached to the Defence motion of 3rd March, year 2003, may be added to the original Defence exhibit list dated 18th November, year 2002, except for the following exhibits where no English translation has yet been provided: 567, 568, 569, 574, 575, 579, 580, 581, 582, 583, 584, 585. In this regard, the Chamber emphasises that there has as yet been no ruling on the admission of any of these documents into evidence. This concludes the procedural section of this afternoon's hearings. We will Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. now continue with the evidence of Mr. Travar. Would the usher please bring the witness in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Travar. The Bench would like to remind you that you are still under the solemn declaration to tell the truth in this courtroom. Please, do sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Koumjian, the floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Questioned by Mr. Koumjian: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the break, we were looking at Exhibit Number S181, English page 34, which we found the B/C/S ends in ERN number 741. Sir, is it correct that Section 15, which begins I believe towards the top of that page, very top of the page, indicates "expenditures from the Prijedor budget for the public security section" and lists the amounts for -- first, funds for the operation of administrative organs; under that section, "employees' salaries"; then "funds for special and other purposes"; and under that is "funds for reserve police forces"; and "funds for equipping the public security station." Would it be correct that these -- this document indicates how the municipality funded portions of the public security station budget at that time?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, let me look at the beginning of this section, if you don't mind, this budget. I'd like to know at which session was it adopted and when was that. May I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. And we're looking at, for the record, the Exhibit S181, which I believe states on the first page that it is the 31st -- dated the 31st of August, 1992, related to the session of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor of the 27th of August, 1992. Would that be correct, sir, from reading the first page?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I saw now that it was the meeting which verified the decisions of the 27th, isn't it, that were taken by the Crisis Staff in the meantime. It is true that this is the budget of the municipality of Prijedor as per groups of revenue for 1992. But I'd like to add that this document and the budget of any municipality, and therefore, of the Municipality of Prijedor, was always adopted in the beginning of the year, and it still is. That is the common practice. As you can see the municipal budget was adopted; however, subsequently, in the latter half of 1992, which means that it could not be adopted earlier. What I'm trying to say in my testimony here, I've already said that there were requests from different organisations and institutions, individuals, who were unable to operate normally because of the shortage of funds and the sources from which they usually obtained those funds or other assets. And that in such cases, they turned to the municipal budget. And these resources were then, depending on their availability, of course, were then granted to them. Yesterday, I tried to explain how it came about that a part of the funds which the public security station had spent and then tried to get this money from the -- from its ministry because that was its normal funding channel. However, at that time, because of the number of difficulties with the funding of both the municipal and republican budget, I suppose they were unable to collect the necessary money for all their expenditures, and then they applied either to the Executive Board or the Crisis Staff. And in line with those individual requests and applications, not only of the public security station, but it also held true of the courts, of the public prosecutor's office, that is, those who were not receiving their regular money from the budget and whose funding was under the exclusive jurisdiction of the republican authorities, as they were unable to get this money, either because there was a shortage of those funds or for whatever reason, they then turned to the municipality severally asking that their requests be met. I say this in order to explain why this is here. As you can see, the budget was adopted only at this session, on the 20th of July, and the decision on the budget and the annual statement are normally adopted, that is, the first decision about the budget, and at the end of the year, the performance is assessed. And that is why the department for budget and finances, as there had been certain expenditures which were out of the ordinary, that is, we were paying those institutions which were not otherwise envisaged, and they had to be included in the budget as the budget needs to be adopted by the assembly. And that is why this is here, because the department for the budget and finances in preparation of this draft budget had already included those expenditures which had been made, that is, which had been paid to this institution on the basis of previous decisions of meetings of the Executive Board or the Crisis Staff. Now, if you allow me to continue --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could please just answer the questions because I do have a lot of them, and we want to be sure to finish your testimony this week. Give us as succinct an answer as you can that accurately and completely answers the question. But please, if you could avoid volunteering information so we can finish this afternoon. If you go back one page, you looked before at the funding for the public security station, that was Section 15, if you begin on the next page, I believe it is Section 10, and just reading the headings of the sections, would it be correct that in Section 10, it's listed "the expenditures for the municipal misdemeanours court" which you just mentioned in your testimony. Skipping 11 and going to 12, section 12 was "the municipal public attorney." Section 13, "the municipal Territorial Defence staff." And then going to -- skipping to Section 16, that would be the lower court. And Section 17, the office of the public prosecutor. Were all of these sections funded in the way that you just explained in your previous answer?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the -- pursuant individual applications of these bodies addressed either to the Executive Board or the Crisis Staff, relevant decisions were taken. And since there were these expenditures -- and that is why in this report that we have here, these expenditures were incorporated. But that is not the -- it was not mandatory under the -- such funding from the municipal budget was not mandatory. But these were individual applications, and that is why I'm saying that they had to be incorporated in this report. And if you allow me, to avoid any misunderstanding, and that is I didn't wanted to explain it, by using an example that I remember, I'm merely trying to develop further this document, I remember basic courts which between April were not getting any salaries or any other money or any operating assets. And therefore, it was decided in the Municipal Assembly to try to earmark certain funds from the municipal budget for these purposes. And such decision was taken. So I remember that, even though that was not mandatory; but since regular funds were not flowing in and the judiciary had to be some -- so at the request of the president of the Executive Board and the president of the Court, these funds were approved under the proviso that when normal conditions were established, if possible, then the municipality would seek to be reimbursed from the republican budget. So this is what I remember now and what I'm telling you now, I'm deducing from what I was just reading here. I told you there were individual expenditures, but they were minimal amounts in relation to the budget because the average salaries were 10 or 20 marks for a judge or somebody from these agencies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Taking that example you just mentioned, do you know, if the judges who were interned, detained in the Omarska, if you continued to fund their salary? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you knew Mr. Marjanovic. Would it be correct that you had a professional and a social relationship with him?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, I met Mr. Marjanovic, and I cooperated with him more in 1993 and 1994, when he was the vice-president of the Executive Board for a while when I was his president. So that is when I came to know him better, but otherwise I did not socialise particularly with him nor are we friends today, I mean outside of work. It was at the time when he worked in the Executive Board that I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in either a professional or a social conversation, did Mr. Marjanovic ever talk to you about the use of the facilities of the Ljubija mine company at the Omarska mine site as a detention camp?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm whether it was Ostoja Marjanovic who told me that, but I knew it. I had the information that a prison was housed in those facilities, but I don't remember whether it was Ostoja who told me about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have any recollection of Mr. Marjanovic complaining about the use of those facilities? Do you or do you not?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't complain. I cannot say that he complained because this is not the kind of conversation I had with Mr. Marjanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, going to the Crisis Staff would you say that the primary purpose of the formation of the Crisis Staff was to disarm extremists armed by the SDA? Was that the reason it was formed?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that this was the reason why the Crisis Staff was established. I tried to tell you what I know about the way it was established and what its tasks were. But I cannot confirm that it was its sole purpose or its main task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, if I could just refer to S83.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps to be fair, that should be shown to the witness. And the next document, just for the Usher -- for the Registrar, would be S192.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While that's being prepared, Mr. Travar, is it correct that in the Crisis Staff, you didn't normally vote on a decision. The president or a presiding officer who propose it, and there would be a consensus to adopt that decision. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've tried to explain how it was. I believe I tried to do that on the first day or on the second day. We did not have the agenda in advance. And as for decision-taking, sometimes people did vote, but most commonly, the question was: "Is there anything against?" And this was the way decisions were taken in the majority of cases. There was no show of hands or voting on any particular item on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that would normally propose the decision?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agenda was established at the sessions of the Crisis Staff. The chair would call the meeting to order and would announce the topics that would be discussed. And if any of the members had something to add to that agenda, the agenda would be amended. And that's the way decisions were taken and that's the way the Crisis Staff worked and conducted its sessions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just to be clear about your answer, I'm not saying that this is inconsistent, but in the interview in Banja Luka, on page 34, line 11, I'm going to read to you the question and answer, and tell me if you believe this accurately describes the procedure. I asked you: "Who would propose the decisions?" And you answered: "This was usually -- they were usually proposed by the presiding person; that is, the president or the person who was presiding at that session." So would that be correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I have just said. It was the president who proposed and established the agenda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Going now to S83, a newspaper article from Kozarski Vjesnik dated the 26th of June, 1992, it includes, if you look for the article called -- with the headline "They called it a civil state, but they have pushed us into the middle ages," do you see, sir, that it includes an interview with Dr. Stakic --

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first answer he gave to the first question -- the first question was: "Exactly 30 days have passed since the formation of the Crisis Staff in Prijedor. What are its main objectives and what is your assessment of its work so far?" Going to the last sentence of Dr. Stakic's answer, you see that he answered: "The primary purpose of the Crisis Staff was to disarm the extremists who had been armed by the SDA." Would you agree with what Dr. Stakic said in that June interview?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to say. I've told you how I perceived the Crisis Staff and the way Dr. Stakic commented upon the functions of the Crisis Staff is entirely up to him. It was entirely his vision. I didn't read this interview before, so that...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Sir, you talked in your testimony about Document S192 concerning abandoned property. I believe you discussed that yesterday at page 37 of the transcript. And you said at that time that, in answer to Mr. Lukic's questions, that the purpose of that decision was to protect the property that had been abandoned. I'm paraphrasing your response. Sorry, just to be clear. I'll read the question and answer. On line 17, Mr. Lukic asked: "Does this corroborate your view that this was done to protect this property?" And you answered: "Well, I said yesterday, I don't know if it's necessary for me to repeat it. I think that the purpose that there is that behind all such acts was to protect this property against all further destruction because it was abandoned." Sir, looking at this decision, it does not apply only to property that was abandoned by persons who left Prijedor, but it also applies, does it not, according to Article 1, to persons who participated in the armed uprising. What do you understand by that phrase "persons who participated in the armed uprising"? Does that apply to the events of the 30th of April? Did that apply to people involved subsequent events?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to comment upon this. It does say unambiguously that all the abandoned property of persons who have left the territory and of persons who participated in the armed rebellion. I really don't know what to say. If I can share my views with you, this means that persons who participated in the rebellion or in the attack, and I really don't know what comments I can offer to you. What I said and what I can confirm is -- although this does not belong to my scope of duties, I only know that the purpose of this decision was to protect the abandoned property to a certain extent from everything that was going on at that time and what I was talking about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, doesn't this decision give a license to the authorities to seize the property, not just of people who had fled Prijedor, but of those who were detained in the Omarska, Keraterm, and Trnopolje camps?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to say. I'm not a lawyer. I cannot comment on this decision. I'm not sure, and I didn't have any information to the effect that property was confiscated from people who lived in it. I really don't know that, and I cannot offer any comment on this decision to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to distribute another document. It was on the 65 ter list under number 322. Part of that 65 ter has been admitted as S107, but this is a separate document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So I think it should be marked probably next in order, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall after the visit of the foreign journalists to Prijedor there being instructions and political instructions from the republic level to report on the camps in the municipality of Prijedor and other areas? Do you recall anything about discussions regarding that?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the document which has hopefully been handed to you, or will be shortly, you'll see from the title is from the Serbian Republic -- perhaps the first page could be put on the ELMO also. Serbian Republic Ministry of the Interior, Security Services Centre, Banja Luka. And it indicates: "Pursuant to the decision of the chief of the Security Services Centre, decision number 11-141/2 of 14 August 1992, the commission for the inspection of the municipalities and Prijedor, Bosanski Novi, and Sanski Most public security stations submits a report concerning the situation as found and questions relating to prisoners, collection centres, resettlement, and the role of the SJB in connection with these activities." The first section deals with Prijedor. And going to the second paragraph under "Reception centres in the municipality," if you can -- I hope you can follow me, and I'll read from the middle of that paragraph. I don't want to read everything. It will take too long. "In order to solve the problem that had arisen, the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Prijedor decided to organise" --

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, I can't find this. Is that on page 1 of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me find the B/C/S, and I'll try to help you.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it. I apologise. It is the last line on that page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I'm sorry, the pagination is different between the English and B/C/S. But thank you. It is the second paragraph, so the last line on the B/C/S, it says: "In order to solve the problem that had arisen, the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Prijedor decided to organise reception and accommodation in the settlement of Trnopolje for persons who sought protection, and that prisoners of war should be held for processing in the building of the Keraterm work organisation, Keraterm RO, in Prijedor, or in the administrative building and workshop of the iron ore mine in Omarska." Sir, if you could go down and follow me with me, I'm now going to go one, two, three, four, five -- five paragraphs down, and that paragraph begins - I'll just read the first sentence - "Pursuant to the decision of the Prijedor Municipality Crisis Staff, the army brought prisoners of war to this facility." And you can see from the preceding paragraph, that was referring to Keraterm. Go down two paragraphs further -- excuse me, one paragraph further, in the middle of the paragraph is says: "At the same time, the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Prijedor assessed it would be advisable for security reasons as well to transfer the prisoners to another place, and decided on the facilities of the administrative building and workshops of the Omarska iron ore mine." The next paragraph begins: "On 27 May 1992, pursuant to the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Prijedor, all the prisoners from the Keraterm...facility were transferred to the facility in Omarska." Sir, were you present when these decisions referred to by the Crisis Staff of Prijedor were made?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that. I said it during my interview in Banja Luka that to my knowledge, no such decisions were taken at the Crisis Staff. And as for this report, if I may share my views with you, this report was drafted by the Ministry of the Interior, the Security Services Centre in Banja Luka set up a commission that was given the task to draft this report. This confirms my belief and my claim that the police used the Crisis Staff in order to blame the Crisis Staff for the things that they didn't do correctly. So this report was drafted by them for their commanding structures. And now I'm even more positive that I was right. When I asked Mr. Kovacevic, like I told you yesterday, to abolish the Crisis Staff because we as a body could not take any decisions. We didn't know anything about these things; we couldn't take any decisions about these things. And this report confirms my views that they made everybody believe that it was the Crisis Staff who made decisions and did things, which was not true. And that is, probably somebody in the police asked for this report to be drafted to the superior structures in the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, in your opinion, would it be correct or incorrect to say that the camps were set up following a decision of the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This cannot be true because the civilian authorities did not take decisions on the establishment of these camps. But I can guess why you're asking me that. In an interview given by Mr. Stakic, this is what he stated. He stated something along these lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever hear Dr. Stakic complain that the police had misused the name of the Crisis Staff? Do you know of any public interview he gave in which -- we could find in which he said that the Crisis Staff had been misused by the police?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have that sort of information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could have S180 brought to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: While that's being done, Your Honour -- could the commission report be marked next in order. Just to correct, I had just stated that the document -- the other part of the document was S107. Ms. Karper has corrected me. It was S152. Perhaps this is a separate document and perhaps should receive a separate number. We would tender it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next Exhibit Number is S407A and B.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May I proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did the Crisis Staff dismiss directors of private- and socially-owned enterprises?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No such decision was taken at the sessions of the Crisis Staff that I attended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, referring to the document S -- I'm sorry, and I believe I...

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can I have S250. I'm sorry. I apologise. I gave the wrong number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we talked about the influence of the Crisis Staff on the army, and particularly on the police. And this document, S250, you will see is the document where the Municipal Assembly confirmed the decisions made by the Crisis Staff between 29 May and 24 July. I want to go through some of those decisions with you. Referring to the enactments, if you have it in front of you, of the 31st of May, you will see that the first conclusion was "prohibiting the return of POWs to Trnopolje and Prijedor." Do you recall this decision and can you explain it to us?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this decision. I did not attend the session at which this decision was adopted. I believe that I've already told you that. I told you that during my interview in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you did tell us I believe yesterday that you were in Belgrade on the 30th of May. When did you return from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether this was on the 30th of May. This is not what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, and I'm confusing also because the 30th of May you said you were home during the attack on Prijedor. Excuse me. The next decision, on the 31st of May --

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next decision on the 31st of May, it relates to people fleeing in Trnopolje. Do you know anything -- can you explain to us what this decision concerned?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I have a look at that decision, if that is not a problem? Because -- is this in this document that I have in front of me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, sir. All we have is what you have in front of you right now regarding that decision. Do you know anything or could you explain to us what this conclusion concerned?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have in front of me is the ratification of decisions adopted by the Crisis Staff on the part of the Municipal Assembly. Is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that the document that you have in mind, that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm referring specifically to enactments passed on 31 May 1992, the second conclusion. It indicates it related to people fleeing in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember this conclusion. I don't know what it contains. I don't know what the discussion was all about. I've already said it, and I abide by what I have said, and that is that at the sessions of the Crisis Staff which I attended, we never adopted any decisions regarding the collection centres or persons detained there or the work of these detention or investigation centres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Crisis Staff or the bodies of which you were a member or attended issue orders to the police that the police then were obligated to enforce?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have had an opportunity to see an order which was signed by the Crisis Staff and which was relative to the establishment of the intervention platoon. This is something you showed me in Banja Luka. I believe that the title of that decision was an order of -- on the establishment of the platoon. During my testimony, I've told you what I think about that order. Why this document was called an order, I don't know. I'm not clear whether the Crisis Staff could issue such a legal enactment pursuant to any of the rules regulating the work of administrative bodies. But I'm sure that this could not have been drafted as an order. Why did the person drafting this document call it an order, I don't know. I really don't know because as I've told you, I did not have any feedback on all the decisions taken by the Crisis Staff. The decisions, once they were drafted, were submitted only to those persons who had to be informed about those decisions. But as I've already told you, at the Crisis Staff sessions, we did discuss the possibility of giving the task to the police to prevent all those things that were happening in the territory of Prijedor Municipality during those days. Maybe this was just an attempt to reinforce that attempt, to make it sound stronger. Maybe that's why this document was called an order. But effectively, the Crisis Staff could not issue any orders to either the police or to the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I understand that, in the interests of time, I'm going to go through this document and just read the titles of specific orders and conclusions that I believe relate to the army and police. And at the end, you can provide any comment; and at the end, I would ask you to then comment about whether or not this is -- contradicts your statement that the Crisis Staff could give no order or have no influence over the army or police. On the enactments on the 5th of July, if you can follow me by the date, the first order was forbidding unauthorised shooting. The fifth order was on procedures by the military police and on the public security station. The ninth order was on the forming of a logistics unit. On the enactments of the 6th of June, the fifth order -- excuse me, was a conclusion -- Number 5 was a conclusion making Crisis Staff members responsible for providing efficient security for the hospital. The seventh item is a conclusion on the continuation of the blockade measures. Going to the 7th of June, the 13th order -- excuse me, 13th item was a conclusion making the regional command responsible --

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not getting the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I was speaking too quickly. Let me try again. Going now to the 9th of June, Mr. Travar, if you can find that, in this particular conclusion I'd like to ask you about in a little bit more detail. The 13th item is conclusion number 02-111-166/92-1, "Making the regional command responsible for transferring the Kozaraputevi equipment to the collection centre in Orlovaca." Sir, why would the Crisis Staff make the regional command responsible for transferring equipment from the Kozaraputevi to the collection centre in Orlovaca? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't, because I have no recollection of this at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Kozaraputevi company was a road-making company, and that their equipment would include earth-digging equipment, earth-moving equipment such as bulldozers?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kozaraputevi, yes, that's right. This was their field of work. And to this day, Kozaraputevi builds roads, and they have the mechanicisation needed for that type of work

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It could be used for building roads or for digging in the earth. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going to the 10th of June, the second item is a conclusion assigning the duty of providing security for the Trnopolje camp to the regional command. I'm sorry, I missed the first item. The first item is a conclusion requesting the municipal secretariat to report on the logistics base. Going to the 12th of June, the fifth conclusion is on -- and the date is the 12th of June, the fifth conclusion is on the liberalisation for the procedure of issuing movement permits to citizens. The eighth conclusion was concerning the continued operation of the logistics base in Cirkin Polje and the provision of food for refugees and prisoners. If I stop for a moment on that conclusion, sir, what prisoners do you believe this conclusion refers to?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say positively, but I presume the prisoners in those prisons that you spoke about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Going to the 16th of June, the first conclusion, assigning members of the Crisis Staff the duty of preparing a system of supplying food to the army and police troops. Going to the --

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which conclusion, sorry?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, the enactments passed on the 16th of June, first conclusion, assigning members of the Crisis Staff the duty of preparing a system of supplying food to the army and police troops. I believe we discussed this the other day, or a similar enactment. Going now to the 17th of June, the fourth item is entitled an order concerning the obligation to report on the procurement of military equipment. I skipped over the first item because that concerns the intervention platoon that we've discussed at quite some length. The 11th item is a conclusion concerning pay for the reserve police force for the month of April 1992. Going to the 23rd of June, the sixth item on 23 June, is a conclusion directed to the regional command to ensure uniformity of the Serbian army insignia. The 11th conclusion -- the 11th item was a conclusion to reject the request submitted by Muharem Dauti, to return to Stari Grad. On the 22nd of June, the third item is a conclusion on responsibility for collecting refugees from Cela, Donja Puharska, and Trnopolje. Going to the 25th of June, the first item is a conclusion adopting a wartime job plan in organs of the municipality, the judiciary and services, and transferring to the adopted plan. Going to the 2nd of July, the first item is a conclusion coordinating the wartime disposition of the military and police. The second item is a conclusion concerning the obligation to pay military and police members. The fourth item is the conclusion previously mentioned prohibiting the individual releases of persons from Trnopolje, Omarska, and Keraterm. Going to the 24th of July, the seventh item, it's entitled, "A decision rationalising the public security service." Sir, given all of these items referring to army or police or law and order, is it still your position or do you have any comment upon the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. ability of the Crisis Staff to influence the army and police?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've told you what my position was. I don't know why. I'd say this is largely due to the ignorance of the competencies of the Crisis Staff by the services which worked for it and the president who -- and the president at the time. I'm quite sure that a large number of these decisions, conclusions, and the rest which have to do with the army and the police could not be taken, and they were not returned as a feedback, nor did we ever discuss the decisions or the previous meetings at a subsequent meeting so that I'm not aware that people talked about these decisions and conclusions, or voted on them. Secondly, the Crisis Staff, since it operated in line with the then-constitution and laws, it could not take decisions which would be legally valid and applicable to the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did Dr. Stakic attend meetings of the Executive Board? Was it common that the president would sometimes attend the meetings of the Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that he was present there and that did not often happen. He was not present there as often as not. I do not remember if he ever attended those meetings, to be more accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be an appropriate time for a break. Yes, it's an appropriate time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until 4.15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, sir, I want to turn now to discuss a little bit about Dr. Stakic. Would it be correct to say that after the takeover on the 30th of April, Dr. Stakic was formally the first person in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Stakic was elected the president, but I think there were people who enjoyed more popularity than he did, such Mr. Kovacevic, for instance, who was more liked about the town than Dr. Stakic. But he was the municipal president, and that makes that office significant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 62 of your interview in Banja Luka, on line 28, you said the following, and you tell me if you believe this is consistent with what you just said: "There were more -- other people who were more famous than him. I met him for the first time when -- on the day I was appointed a member of the Executive Board, but he was formally the first person of the municipality. At the time, he was the president." And you were referring to Dr. Stakic. Is that consistent with what you've told us? Do you agree with that, what you said in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I've just repeated, except that in Banja Luka, perhaps I gave you a more extensive answer as I had the idea that the first time I saw him at the assembly session, it was the first time I saw him, when I was elected member of the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when this government took power after the 30th of April, would it be correct that it was important that the government be viewed as legitimate, at least in the eyes of the Serbian population, and that the selection of Dr. Stakic, who had been elected the vice-president in the 1990 elections, was a logical choice in order to give legitimacy to that body?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I believe, yes, there was such a view. When the Serb councilmen left the Municipal Assembly, the Serb Assembly was legalised because the -- in the republican parliament, the Serb MPs had also walked out from it because all those who had been elected were elected to the mixed assembly. And those who walked out, they continued working in the other assembly apart from my office, and I was appointed to it instead of Mr. Dragic, who was on the front and therefore was not there. But at this tier of authority, the legislative power, all councilmen who were Serbs and who had walked out of the mixed assembly became members of that new assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just mentioned Mr. Dragic. Just to be clear, is it correct that when you took over the position of the secretary for the secretariat for economy, Mr. Dragic moved over to being the secretary of the secretariat for communal services?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the manager of the public amenities administration, not the secretary for public amenities for public services. These are two different things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction. Do you recall Dr. Stakic giving a speech after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember him speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to see if I can refresh your recollection, let me turn to page 55 of the interview in Banja Luka. Actually, I'll give you the question on the bottom of page 54. Let's begin with line 31 on page 54. We were talking about Cirkin Polje. "Was Stakic at that house?" You answered: "I think he was." I asked: "Did you hear him give a speech the next morning on the radio?" You answered: "I think that was a declaration, and that Stakic spoke to the people about two or three days later, but I can't really tell you because I didn't even listen that speech. I don't remember. I know that he did speak to people." Does that refresh your recollection or would that be accurate that you think he gave a speech a few days after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not listening to that speech, so I cannot say whether there was such a speech or not. But after talking with my colleagues, I had a feeling, that is, I learned that he addressed. But I do not know whether it was two, three, or five days later. I cannot confirm that after all this time. But even then I said that I did not really remember, that I did not remember whether I saw him in Cirkin Polje. I said that I thought that he had been there, but it's difficult to speak about that. After all this time, it is difficult for me to talk about this because I did not know all these people as well personally at that time. Later on in my work, I came to know them better. But I'm afraid to confuse some events which happened later on rather than at the time that we're talking about, and that is why I'm saying that I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Would it be accurate to describe Dr. Stakic as a person who enjoyed public speaking and giving interviews to the media? Did he appear often in the media?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not know how often he appeared in the media, but I think that even that first statement when you asked me about that, I think that I said that then, that because he was very inexperienced. And very often when journalists would insist, he agreed to give interviews at times even about things that he was not familiar enough with in view of his inexperience. I think he often communicated with the media, and I suppose it was the office that at that time he held required. But I didn't have really much opportunity to follow his appearances in the media. But I did come across his interviews in the press.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to page 75 of the interview in Banja Luka, beginning on line 24, you stated: "He really like being on TV, on radio, having things to say in the papers. And he liked -- he liked to publicise, to state his views publicly in the media." The question was regarding Dr. Stakic's attitude towards the non-Serb population. Would that be accurate what you said -- what I just read as far as you recall about Dr. Stakic's appearances in the media?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right. I repeated something along those lines this time, too. Because he was very young at the time, perhaps he appeared in the media more than was necessary, and I suppose whenever journalists asked him to, he would agree to that and give them an interview. But I cannot confirm positively how much and how often. But it was my impression that perhaps he appeared more than necessary or more than he meant at the time, more than he stood for at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you go to Dr. Stakic's office and meet with him privately Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. regarding municipal business, not as part of the Crisis Staff or Executive Board, but just you and him?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. The posts that we held did not turn the two of us to each other. One of us was a member of the executive power, and the other legislative power. But the president did have a possibility to call me and consult me on an issue pertaining to my office. I don't know whether he did, and I don't know how many times he did that. In any case, we never held a private conversation. There were always some other people present, either his secretary or some other people. If he wanted to know something about finances, then yes, I would go there to clarify one thing or another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, just for the record, a testimony -- a witness testified in this case, Ostoja Radakovic, on page 11.090 of the transcript, she was asked: "Would you call, to come to meetings, Ranko Travar for Dr. Stakic?" She said: "Yes, those were not meetings, they were just briefings. He was the head of finance department and was a very important secretariat for everyday life." Would you agree that the secretary for Dr. Stakic, or the receptionist, would call you sometimes to come to his office for briefings of Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who invited me, but it was my receptionist who informed me. So it would be Dr. Stakic's receptionist who would call my secretary, and then my secretary would simply tell me that I was wanted by the president. I don't remember his receptionist calling my direct number at any time. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember -- recall that after the takeover of power, when Dr. Stakic moved from vice-president to president, did he then begin to drive or be driven in a Mercedes automobile?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether he had a driver or whether he drove himself. But yes, there was a Mercedes, a Mercedes was a car that Dr. Stakic was using. But I don't remember whether he was driven or whether he drove it himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he took over that position as president, did his housing change? Did he get an apartment in Prijedor town as a result of having that position?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was given an apartment. I know that he resolved his housing problem, but when that happened, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "he resolved the problem," we're not -- I'm not quite clear on that. Do you mean he was able to move from Omarska into the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did get an apartment, but I don't know when. Whether it was immediately following his taking this office or at some later stage. In any case, he did move into the town of Prijedor, and that is what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Simo Drljaca before the meeting of the 16th of April where you were elected to the secretariat?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that same meeting that you were elected, Mr. Drljaca was elected as the chief of the public security service in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that because I don't know whether it was at all possible for Mr. Drljaca to be appointed or -- I believe it was either the minister or the chief of the public services centre who appointed him. I don't know whether it was within the competence of the assembly to appoint anybody to that position. So I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher could get S262.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that the law says that the minister of the interior appoints the chief of police. But in fact, at the same meeting where you were elected, on the same ballots was Simo Drljaca for chief of the public security station. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will look at the document. I said that I don't remember. I know that Mr. Drljaca was there, but maybe you can give me the opportunity to take a look at the copy of the minutes of that session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly, I'll try to find the correct page. I believe in English, it would be ERN number 03024254. And in B/C/S, I believe it's P0038608. P0038608.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here under 5 that the following members have been elected by secret ballot. The members of the Executive Board, I don't know what this "VD" stands for. I believe this is acting officers. And then what follows is a list of people. So that means that he was elected, but whether the assembly had the legal right to do that, I don't think so. What I think is that the assembly just confirmed or established its proposal for its candidate, that it was then to forward towards the competent ministry that would appoint the person. Let me tell you, I'm not familiar with this at all, so I can't say anything positively. I can't confirm anything positively about that. As far as I know, the assembly did not have the possibility to appoint chiefs of public security centres or any other such institutions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, on the same document, it indicates on the same ballot, in addition to Mr. Budimir, number 2; yourself, number 3; on the 11th position, Slobodan Kuruzovic was appointed TO staff commander. Number 13, Mico Kreco, president of the court; and number 15, Milenko Tomic, public prosecutor. Would it be correct for these three positions, similar to what you told us about Mr. Drljaca, that although the legal requirements were these be appointed at a higher level, they were elected and proposed for this decision -- for these positions by the local authorities at that meeting on the 16th of April of the Serbian Assembly?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise answer to this question. I adhere to my previous statement. I know that members of the Executive Board were elected, that they were appointed by the assembly, and that this was in keeping with the law. And as for the rest of this document, whether these were just proposals to be forwarded to the competent institutions for the final appointment, I really can't say. I can't give you a precise answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Drljaca immediately after the takeover assume the position of chief of police? Did Mr. Kuruzovic assume the position of the TO commander? Mr. Kreco president of the Court? And Mr. - I believe his name is - Tomic the position as the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they took those offices on the following day. I know that Mr. Kreco was in the court. I believe that he was the president of the court later on. I know that because he came to see me about the issues relative to the payment of the salaries of court officials in May, June, and July. Milenko Tomic, he was a prosecutor for a long time. But whether he took the office immediately after this assembly or whether he waited to be appointed by the competent institution at some later stage, I really don't know. I can't remember, so I can't say anything positive about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to the summons interview -- the interview in Banja Luka, on page 44, do you recall that Mr. Malik asked you: "Did you ever see any conflicts between Kovacevic, Stakic, and Drljaca, anything they disagreed upon?" And you answered: "Not personally. I was never personally present." Would that be correct, you never personally saw any conflicts between these three individuals?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there were no conflicts, although Mr. Drljaca was very short-tempered. He was not easy to work with; therefore, it is possible that there may have been some skirmishes. But I wouldn't call those conflicts. In any case, I did not witness any conflicts among them. But I know that every time Mr. Simo Drljaca came to a session, he would address all of us in very harsh words; that is, all of us who wanted to ask him any questions or wanted to learn anything about what was going on around us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that Mr. Drljaca came very often to the meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how often. He didn't attend all the meetings of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Crisis Staff. How often he did, I don't know. I can't even remember how many sessions I attended. But I know that he did not attend some of the sessions that I attended. In any case, I really don't know how often he attended those sessions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 42, line 25, you were asked by Mr. Malik in Banja Luka: "How often was Drljaca present at the meetings? We ask that to you again. Could you again explain how frequently he was there." You responded: "He did come. He didn't come to every meeting that I attended. But what I could say is: He did come very often. He came often." Would you stand by that answer?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you have as translation. I've just told you that he did attend the sessions. He didn't attend all the sessions that I attended. So my answer would be that often, he did not attend the same sessions I did. So I can't give you an exact number as to how many sessions he attended, whether he attended them often or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Drljaca was a lawyer who worked for the schools and not a professional policeman prior to the takeover. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that from my colleagues. I didn't know that, but that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Dr. Stakic was forced out of office in early 1993, Mr. Drljaca was also at the same time forced out of the position of head of the public security station. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I believe I have a document regarding that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Could this be distributed, Your Honour. It would be a new document. It has the ERN number in English of 00467081, and 7082, two pages. It is the first two pages of the Gazette from 1993 dated the 26th of March 1993. And in B/C/S -- I think we have the wrong B/C/S, at least on the copy that I have. Let me check what the usher has, because this doesn't appear to be the same. I'll have Ms. Karper check on that. Apparently the B/C/S appears to me to be the wrong attachment. I'll skip that, Your Honour. Thank you, we'll get that another day. Your Honour, just moving on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in 1997, do you recall that Mr. Drljaca was killed in an attempted arrest? And isn't it correct that you at that time were a minister of the government and attended a commemoration, a ceremony, honouring Mr. Drljaca in Banja Luka on the 13th of July 1997?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a minister at that time, and I did attend this commemoration service. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that ceremony, there was a very large number of people in attendance. Is that correct? Perhaps 2.000.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many people were at the commemoration, but at the funeral, there were a lot of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that several speeches were made on the 13th at the commemorative session, and that among those who spoke was Dr. Stakic, and Ranko Mijic, who was the then chief of the Prijedor police?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Dr. Stakic did speak, but I can't remember about Mr. Mijic giving a speech.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that Dr. Stakic said words to the effect of "although Simo Drljaca was killed, his great work will live on for the benefit of future generations"?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember what was said in the speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Finally, if the witness can now be shown I believe it is S114. Let me double check that. S114.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document as a report to the Crisis Staff dated the 1st of July signed by Simo Drljaca regarding the implementation of various decisions, conclusions, and orders of the Crisis Staff by the public security station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Baltic indicated that he was requested by the Crisis Staff to obtain this information from Mr. Drljaca. Does that refresh your recollection that the Crisis Staff asked or Dr. Stakic asked for a report on the implementation of the Crisis Staff decisions?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that this was ever requested or that Mr. Baltic prepared a report. I don't remember. I can't confirm that this was ever discussed at the Crisis Staff meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. Further questions by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, I would like to clarify one issue: In this famous Banja Luka interview in March of year 2002, answering the question of Mr. Koumjian which side of the Plavsic/Karadzic split did Stakic take - this is pages 74, 75 - you answered: "I don't really know, but he stayed on Karadzic's side. This is my personal opinion because at that time I didn't see Mr. Stakic very often because I had moved to Banja Luka. But he stayed within the SDS." Do you confirm this statement?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by this. This is what I said in answer to Mr. Prosecutor's question. I said I was not sure which political option he continued to support, but I thought that he had remained with the SDS. It was at that time that I left the SDS, so I cannot be sure whether he stayed with the SDS to the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Within the SDS on Karadzic's side, yes? It's your opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is my opinion. I don't know. Mr. Karadzic withdrew from all offices, including the post of the president of the party. I don't know whether it was, whether it was in 1995 or 1996 or 1997. What I remember are the events that took place in 1997, when I was a minister of finances, and I remember the conflict that Mrs. Plavsic had with the leadership of the SDS, the government, the presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you for your clarification. Judge Argibay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, today you were discussing at page 25 of your testimony all the competencies of the Crisis Staff, and looking at a lot of decisions, resolutions, orders, whatever you want to call them, that you say were not discussed at the Crisis Staff meeting. So there must be an abuse of the Crisis Staff name, at least, or authority to pass that. Can you tell me, who was the president of the Municipal Assembly on July the 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 24 July 1992, it was Mr. Stakic who was the president of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: And Mr. Stakic also -- Dr. Stakic, was the president of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: So how is it possible that the president of the Crisis Staff will submit to the assembly as the president of the Municipal Assembly decisions, orders, resolutions, whatever you want to call them, of the Crisis Staff that were not truly passed by the Crisis Staff, if he was the same person, and he was not telling the Municipal Assembly to deny that orders but asking them to ratify these resolutions of the Crisis Staff? Can you explain me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my today's testimony, I said that many decisions that were mentioned here did not pertain to the area of the responsibility of the assembly, which means that they did not pertain to the area of responsibility of the Crisis Staff because the Crisis Staff stood instead of the Assembly. Many issues were discussed at the Crisis Staff without the predetermined agenda and without any feedback being provided to all the members of the Crisis Staff. That's why I was not familiar with all the decisions that were taken by the Crisis Staff, but Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. there were a number of decisions which were submitted to the assembly for ratification which did not pertain to the area of responsibility of either the assembly or the Crisis Staff because they could not be sent to the bodies that they were sent to. I've tried to explain that by saying that people working in the legal affairs of the Municipal Assembly were just not doing their job properly, and they did not articulate well those things that were under the authority of the assembly. And they would draft decisions, conclusions, and orders, and then they would give those to the president to sign. And when there were a number of such documents or decisions or amendments, they would collectively be submitted to the assembly for ratification by that same president.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Are you telling me that the assembly just ratified all the documents, decisions, orders, that they were presented with without the president of the assembly telling them about what you called this afternoon an abuse of the authority of the Crisis Staff? Is that what you're meaning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, as far as I can remember, there were -- there was no reasoning at that assembly. The decisions were read and adopted as such so that the individual decisions were not discussed. They were simply listed. So there were no warnings about somebody's lack of jurisdiction of either the assembly or the Crisis Staff over the decisions that were taken and related to those which ought not to have been taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Is the Defence willing to ask additional questions --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Is the Defence willing to ask additional questions related to the matters raised by the Judges?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have a few questions emanating from the questions of Your Honours and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Yes, the floor is yours. Further questions by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Travar, good afternoon once again.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for keeping you here, but we need to clarify certain things which arise from the questions by Their Honours and our learned friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness first be shown Document S406.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, the Prosecutor showed you this document, and at that time, I tried to object. But it is a fact that for these supplementary questions, it is the time and the place to clear up certain moot points, so that I will ask you now whether this document was signed by Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin? Can you see that in this document?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that this document you did not sign either, even though you're indicated here as one of the signatories?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I did not remember this document, and my signature is missing here so I don't know. But I did not sign, not this copy. And I do not remember having ever seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document that I'd like to ask you about is a document which the Prosecution has not tendered so far, and I do not know if it was given a number today, and that is the report of the commission of the public security centre in Banja Luka. Public security centre in Banja Luka, that was the commission which was headed by Mr. Vojin Bera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that it is S407. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor has explained that this was in point of fact the second part of the document with the number S107. And this document is S407. I won't go into the analysis of these two documents with you now, but they are almost verbatim identical even though one of them was allegedly written by Simo Drljaca, and the other one by the Security Services Centre, rather the commission that was set up. Today, we heard that Simo Drljaca was a lawyer by education. As you go through this document, did you ever see the commission which used Simo Drljaca's report ever use any number or the decision or the alleged decision of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no opportunity to read this document in toto. But these parts that were pointed out by the Prosecutor, it did not say that. That is, on the third page and second it says: "On the basis of the Crisis Staff decision," and there is no number there attached to it. But I want to say that during this testimony here, he also showed me a document on the basis of which Mr. Drljaca was ordering something, and that document was also lacking a number. So that I don't know. From this report, from those parts which were read out to me, there were no decisions that Mr. Drljaca had been referring to, or this commission. I don't know which of the two reports you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the police -- that after the visit to the investigation centres of the foreign journalists, a broad campaign of concealment was started with regard to all the things that the police had been doing in those investigation centres?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I knew nothing about the visit of those international journalists or the visit of any foreign team in this area, least of all do I know whether somebody tried to conceal anything. I don't know. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether this commission headed by Vojin Bera ever turned to the Crisis Staff when it wrote this report?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know Mr. Bera. He did not turn to us, nor did he come to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Bera, in his report, on page 5 of the B/C/S version said the following: "Over 3.334 persons brought into custody to the investigation centre in Omarska, between the 27th of May and the 16th of August, 1992, Muslims accounted for 1.820-something; Croats, 125; 11 Serbs; the rest, 1 -- and others, 1. During their stay in the investigation centre, two persons of Muslim ethnicity died of natural causes, and 49 persons left the investigation centre in an unknown manner." Have you ever heard the police claim that in the Omarska investigation centre, two persons died altogether, and even they of natural causes?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not heard this. I'm not aware of this. And I am not familiar with this whole report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We won't be needing this document any more, but I'd like the witness to be shown the Document S265.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not interested in the contents of this document. All I'm going to ask you is whether at the bottom of this document it says that it was signed by Mr. Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this document have a reference to a number and a date to which this reply relates?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the upper left corner?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Drljaca was not unaware of the obligation to refer to a number and the date of a document to which he's referring? Can we conclude that from this document?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't really understand your question. I tried to read what it said here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. Since you know that Mr. Drljaca has a degree in law, can one deduce from this document that as somebody with a law degree, he was aware that when he was referring to a document by another agency, that it was necessary to indicate the number and the date of the document to which he would be referring to? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We won't need this document any longer. [In English] I would like the usher now to show the witness the Document Number S63 [Realtime transcript read in error "S163"], please. Sorry, S63. Because in the transcript, I can see S163. Probably my English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Travar, the Prosecutor asked you something about this document, and I will merely in pursuant of further clarification ask you whether this document has a seal.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this document signed?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this document have a number in the upper left corner?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this document have a date?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we know what is this document?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says it's the request of the Autotransport for the reimbursement of costs, but what you have just listed is missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that common in our practice, to use such documents?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like now the usher to show the witness the Exhibit Number S181, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, can you turn to page 106, and the only difference I see is in the numbers that stand immediately next to the text. So above number 8, the title is "means for other social needs or requirements."

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please read what the payments were made for on the numbers between 8 and 15 on the following page, and can you do it slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Payments for local communes, 2.091.847. Payments for social, political, and other organisations, a total 1.504.923, out of which the Executive Board of the Serbian Democratic party, 34.875." I apologise. "The municipal board of the Party of Democratic Action," that is. "The municipal board of the SDS, 1.221.835. Socialist democratic party, 91.926. The municipal board of the reformist forces, 101.918. The municipal board of the democratic alliance party, 34.747. The municipal board of the HDZ, 2.321."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 15 on the following page?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read it in my copy. I don't have it in my copy. It's missing. There's no number 15 in my copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
